cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's exfoliant shortcut with the hidden-preservative possibility.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 restate opening positions instead of answering T6's afraid-to-use point.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 adds that stopping everything leaves the user afraid of three products; T9 partly uses it.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8 add nothing beyond T1 and T2; development stalls after T6.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T1, T2, T5 examine rigor versus speed versus repeated inflammation.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises product interaction, irritant versus allergic reaction, or when to see a clinician.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 combines stopping, healing and testing the most suspicious item.
cells.limitation: T9 merges views alone; Reductionist and Risk Manager never qualify their positions in response.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T9 and section E end with a usable sequence: stop, heal, test.
cells.limitation: Section D reframes the outcome as truth versus safety values, not a sharper open question.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 represents T3's culprit-first shortcut accurately before objecting.
cells.limitation: T8 recasts T6's fear-of-use point as saving a few dollars.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5 objects that one-by-one reintroduction risks repeated inflammation.
cells.limitation: T7 never answers T5's repeated-inflammation objection; it restates the need for isolation.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's Bacon paraphrase closely matches a Novum Organum aphorism, without quotation marks.
cells.limitation: T5's long-term sensitivity claim and T8's discard-everything advice go unsupported.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T5 hedges: reintroduction could lead to long-term sensitivity.
cells.limitation: T8 calls discarding the batch the most robust strategy with no evidence offered.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 concedes the user requires relief.
cells.limitation: T7's concession narrows nothing; T3 never answers T4's preservative objection.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A separates immediate relief from identifying the irritant.
cells.limitation: Section D turns a how-to question into truth-versus-safety values the user never voiced.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 and T9 build the plan around three simultaneous new products.
cells.limitation: The one-week timing and stinging symptom never change any argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T6 keeps the user's likely wish to eventually use the products.
cells.limitation: T8 discards the user's stated goal of finding the cause.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T5 weighs repeated inflammation; section E weighs product cost.
cells.limitation: T8 invents that the products are cheap: saving a few dollars.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on inflamed versus merely uncomfortable skin.
cells.limitation: Product types, severity signs and ingredients are never asked; T3's exfoliant case stays hypothetical.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D names valuing the truth of the cause versus skin safety.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered with a question the user can answer.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 exposes the assumption that the exfoliant must be the culprit.
cells.limitation: The assumption of a single culprit, not a combination, is never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T9 names safety, knowledge and practical use as competing aims.
cells.limitation: Where these conflict for this user is asserted in D, not explored.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 notes the user may be left afraid to use the products.
cells.limitation: Worry about lasting damage or appearance is never explored beyond T6's line.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E leaves the choice to the user's own skin condition.
cells.limitation: No question or distinction offered for the user to accept or refine.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options span stop all, reintroduce, target suspect, discard, patch test (T1-T9, E).
cells.limitation: Seeing a dermatologist or professional patch testing is never offered as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5 costs reintroduction in inflammation; T6 costs stopping in unusable products.
cells.limitation: Costs of the inner-arm patch test, such as arm skin differing from facial skin, unstated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T3: a harsh exfoliant among mild hydrators marks a clear candidate.
cells.limitation: No observable sign for when to seek care or when skin counts as healed.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T4 flags a possible preservative reaction in a hydrator.
cells.limitation: Irritant versus allergic reaction and product interaction, the consequential unknowns, never separated.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T9: stop all three, heal, test the most suspicious item on a small area.
cells.limitation: No escalation step if stinging worsens, swells or persists.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T9 states the plan in plain everyday terms.
cells.limitation: T2's stop the bleeding and noise metaphors are slightly abstract for skincare.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T5 names The Reductionist before objecting.
cells.limitation: T9's middle path does not say which turns it reconciles.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within the word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: Near-identical turn lengths give a flat, unvaried rhythm.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Rigor (T1), avoidance (T2), likely-culprit pragmatism (T3) are clearly distinct.
cells.limitation: No mind explicitly changes position; registers are similar across all three.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T4 adds a new consideration rather than recapping.
cells.limitation: T7 repeats T1 and T4; T8 repeats T2 and T5.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T5 sets lasting sensitivity against information gathering.
cells.limitation: Tension stays abstract; the user's actual stinging face is rarely evoked.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T7's concession that the user requires relief.
cells.limitation: No reversal; T7's concession names no cause and changes nothing.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T1's Bacon opens bluntly: You have created a muddle.
cells.limitation: T3, T6, T9 read as generic advice with little Jamesian voice.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5: treats the face like a machine in a lab.
cells.limitation: Few vivid examples; most lines are generic maxims.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T9 resolves the standoff with a middle path.
cells.limitation: Even intensity throughout; T7 and T8 stall momentum before T9.

strengths: T4 raises a real alternative cause, a preservative in a hydrator, against T3's exfoliant shortcut.
T5 and T6 surface genuine costs of both reintroduction and total abstention.
T9 and section E deliver a concrete, safe sequence: stop, heal, test separately.
weaknesses: No mind raises product interaction, irritant versus allergic reaction, or when to see a clinician (T1-T9).
The user is never asked what the products are or how severe the stinging is (T3, section E).
T7 and T8 restate opening positions; the Reductionist never answers T5's repeated-inflammation objection.

symptoms.observed: No mind considers that two products together, not one alone, cause stinging.
symptoms.evidence: If you do not isolate the variable

symptoms.observed: Product types and severity never asked; T3's exfoliant case stays hypothetical.
symptoms.evidence: If one product is a harsh exfoliant

symptoms.observed: T7's concession ignores T5's objection and restates T1 unchanged.
symptoms.evidence: I concede that the user requires relief

symptoms.observed: No sign given for when skin has healed or when to seek care.
symptoms.evidence: wait for the skin to heal

symptoms.observed: Middle path arrives with no mind changing position for a stated reason.
symptoms.evidence: Perhaps the middle path is to stop all three

findings.description: No turn or branch names warning signs (swelling, blistering, hives, spreading) that call for medical care.
Invents that the products are cheap and recommends discarding all three without evidence.
Claim that reintroduction leads to long-term sensitivity is stated without support.
Bacon paraphrase resembles the Novum Organum aphorism on nature's subtlety; appears faithful, unconfirmed.

rubric_fit_notes: The troubleshooting question is practical; criterion 4 has limited natural material, so low C4 ratings partly reflect the task, though the debate also missed available motives such as fear of lasting damage.
